title: Rational and common-stage descent of the point Hom comparison
statement:
Fix $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, and finite coefficient fields $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ in a fixed $\Qlb$, with valuation rings $R_E=\mathcal O_E$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber, def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. On $s_{\mathrm{proet}}$ put $B_E=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,s}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Use the raw rational and common-stage point categories and the evaluation functor $F_\Lambda=\operatorname{Fib}_s$ [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point, def-weil-rationalization-karoubi, def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]. For $C\in D^b_c(s,R_E)$ [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], set $c=\Gamma(s,C)$ and choose any bounded finite-projective model $P$ of $c$ [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex]. Identify $C$ with $B_E\otimes_{\underline{R_E}}\underline P$ through the specified extension/sections counit [lem-pod-point-sections-reconstruction], using [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Use the exact extension/sections adjunction and coefficient identification of [lem-pod-point-exact-extension-sections]. Let
$$H_E(C)=R\mathcal Hom_{B_E}(C,B_E),\qquad j_C:\Gamma(s,H_E(C))\xrightarrow{\sim}R\operatorname{Hom}_{R_E}(c,R_E)$$
be the ordinary derived internal Hom and its natural Hom-complex comparison [def-pur-derived-internal-hom, lem-pod-point-derived-hom-evaluation]. Suppose $H_E(C)$ is in $D^b_c(s,R_E)$ and is identified with $B_E\otimes_{\underline{R_E}}\underline{\operatorname{Hom}_{R_E}^\bullet(P,R_E)}$ by the canonical finite-projective Hom model. Internal Hom at rational and common-stage coefficients is that of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. Then the composite of $j_C\otimes_{R_E}E$ with the canonical perfect-source coefficient-Hom base-change arrow along $\mathcal O_E\to E$ [def-pc-perfect-rhom-base-change-map] is an isomorphism in $D(E)$,
$$j^{\mathrm{rat}}_{E,C_E}:F_E(R\mathcal Hom_E(C_E,E_s))\xrightarrow{\sim}R\operatorname{Hom}_E(F_EC_E,E).$$
Here $C_E$ is the rational image of $C$. This arrow is independent of $P$ and is natural for every localized morphism $\sum_i u_i\otimes a_i$, with precomposition by $u_i$ and multiplication by $a_i$ on both sides. For every finite extension $E\subset L$, the square comparing $j^{\mathrm{rat}}_{E,C_E}\otimes_E L$ with $j^{\mathrm{rat}}_{L,C_E\otimes_E L}$ commutes, using exactly the internal-Hom scalar comparison and the point sections comparison specified in [lem-pod-point-scalar-hom-evaluation, lem-weil-point-sections-scalar-extension]. These squares obey the identity and successive-extension cocycles. Consequently the finite-stage arrows give a natural isomorphism
$$F_{\Qlb}(R\mathcal Hom_{\Qlb}(C,\Qlb_s))\xrightarrow{\sim}R\operatorname{Hom}_{\Qlb}(F_{\Qlb}C,\Qlb)$$
in the common-stage point category for every $C$ represented by such an integral model. The right side is computed at the same finite coefficient field as $C$, and the arrow is independent of the chosen stage and of the representative of each common-stage morphism.

proof.text: Put $R=R_E$ and $P^\vee=\operatorname{Hom}_R^\bullet(P,R)$. The exact extension/sections adjunction and the natural counit identify $C$ with $L_RP$ and its sections with $P$ in the derived category. Apply the natural derived Hom comparison to this counit: it gives the specified $j_C$, represented on Hom complexes by $h\mapsto(x\mapsto h(1\otimes x))$. Thus this comparison is intrinsic to $C$, natural on derived morphisms, rather than a choice of a map attached to $P$. The assumed finite-projective model for $H_E(C)$ makes both its rational image and the internal Hom in the rational point category well typed.

source.place: Second sentence: '$R\mathcal Hom$ at the point being computed over the coefficient ring'; returned proof step 7, rationalization and common-stage naturality of the specified Hom comparison

proof.text: Apply perfect-source RHom base change to $R\to E$, first argument $c$ and second argument $R[0]$. The hypothesis is exactly the given bounded finite-projective representative $P$. In the normalized model the base-change arrow is $\beta_{E/R,P}:P^\vee\otimes_RE\to(P\otimes_RE)^\vee$, $\beta(f\otimes a)(x\otimes b)=f(x)ab$. The perfect-dual scalar calculus identifies this as an isomorphism, natural in the perfect derived object and independent of its representative; localization preserves quasi-isomorphisms. The definition of the canonical RHom arrow uses this same pure-tensor map. Consequently $j^{\mathrm{rat}}_{E,C_E}=\beta_{E/R,c}(j_C\otimes_RE)$ is the asserted isomorphism. Its source is $F_E(R\mathcal Hom_E(C_E,E_s))$ by the definitions of rational internal Hom and point evaluation. Independence of $P$ follows from that of $j_C$ and $\beta$, not from selecting an identification between two models.

proof.text: Write $A_E(C)=F_E(R\mathcal Hom_E(C,E_s))$ and $D_E(C)=R\operatorname{Hom}_E(F_EC,E)$, both contravariant. For an integral morphism $u:C\to C'$, naturality from the previous steps says $j^{\mathrm{rat}}_C A_E(u)=D_E(u)j^{\mathrm{rat}}_{C'}$. Every rational morphism is a finite sum $v=\sum_i u_i\otimes a_i$. Rational internal Hom acts by precomposition and point evaluation acts by the specified scalar-linear extension, so $A_E(v)=\sum_i a_iA_E(u_i)$ and $D_E(v)=\sum_i a_iD_E(u_i)$. Multiply the integral equations by $a_i$ and add. This proves naturality for $v$. Tensor balancing makes these actions and this equation independent of the tensor presentation; no torsion-freeness of integral Hom groups is used.

proof.text: For $E\subset L$, use the internal-Hom scalar arrow and sections comparisons specified in the statement. The point scalar-Hom comparison says their integral square is precisely the module map $\beta_{R_L/R_E,P}$, and explicitly asserts its rationalized square and identity/tower compatibilities. The sections comparison identifies the rationalized sections with $F_E(-)\otimes_EL$. Under these identifications the two paths for our $j^{\mathrm{rat}}$ are the successive dual base-change maps along $R_E\to E\to L$ and $R_E\to R_L\to L$, preceded by $j_C\otimes L$. The perfect-dual tower equation identifies each with the direct $R_E\to L$ map. On tensors both send $(f\otimes a,x\otimes b)$ to $f(x)ab$. Hence the square for the actual specified arrows commutes. Identity and successive-extension equations follow from the cited identity/tower equations for the scalar-Hom and sections maps and for $\beta$; their intervening comparison isomorphisms cancel.

proof.text: Use the literal common-stage Hom colimits in the source and target point categories. At $(E,C)$ take the class of $j_E=j^{\mathrm{rat}}_{E,C}$. For a common field $L$, let $a_C:A_L(C_L)\xrightarrow{\sim}A_E(C)\otimes_EL$ and $d_C:D_L(C_L)\xrightarrow{\sim}D_E(C)\otimes_EL$ be the specified scalar comparisons. Step 4 says $d_Cj_{L,C_L}=(j_E\otimes L)a_C$. For a morphism represented by $u:C_L\to C'_L$, the two contravariant functor maps are represented by $a_CA_L(u)a_{C'}^{-1}$ and $d_CD_L(u)d_{C'}^{-1}$. Substitute the preceding scalar equation into the naturality equation of step 3 over $L$; it gives naturality for these conjugated maps. If a representative or initial field changes, pass to a further common field where the representatives agree. Step 4 and its tower equation give the identical conjugated equation there, so the classes agree. The inverse components are the classes of $j_E^{-1}$: both inverse identities already hold at $E$ and therefore in the colimit. This proves stage independence, representative independence and the asserted common-stage natural isomorphism, with its right side computed at the input's finite field.
